operators.name: Robi
operators.note: Robi Axiata's own network. International form: 88018…, 88016…

operators.name: Airtel
operators.note: Airtel Bangladesh, operated by Robi Axiata since the 2016 merger. Shares the 016 series.

baseUrls.configuration: Configure one URL per provisioned service (BDAPPS_SMS_SEND_URL, BDAPPS_USSD_SEND_URL, …). An unset endpoint means that API is not enabled on the application, and the client should refuse to call it rather than fail with E1309 at the platform. See templates/.env.example.

auth.note: Every outbound request carries applicationId and password in the JSON body. There are no headers, tokens or signatures.

rules: Always tel:-prefixed, no + and no spaces. Bangladesh MSISDNs are in international form: tel:8801812345678.
May be a masked hash (tel:hu3b84346f...) when number masking is provisioned. Treat as opaque.
tel:all broadcasts to the entire subscribed base (SMS send only).

responseEnvelope.criticalNote: bdapps returns HTTP 200 for application-level failures. Branch on statusCode, never on the HTTP status alone. S1000 is success.

currency.note: Only BDT is accepted by the CaaS APIs.

services.name: SMS Send
services.summary: Send an MT (Mobile Terminated) SMS to one or more subscribers.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Application ID as given when provisioned.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password given when provisioned.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: API version (1.0, 2.0). Defaults to latest.

parameters.name: destinationAddresses
parameters.description: Array of tel:-prefixed addresses. Always an array, even for one recipient. tel:all targets the whole subscribed base.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Message body. Over-length messages are split by the platform and charged per part.

parameters.name: sourceAddress
parameters.description: Sender address shown to the user — your allocated shortcode (e.g. "77000") or a provisioned tel: alias. Must be provisioned or the send fails with E1331.

parameters.name: deliveryStatusRequest
parameters.description: 0 = no delivery report, 1 = request one. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: encoding
parameters.description: 0 = Text, 240 = Flash SMS, 245 = Binary (message hex-encoded). Defaults to Text.

parameters.name: binaryHeader
parameters.description: Hex-encoded UDH for advanced binary messages. Only meaningful with encoding 245.

responseFields.name: destinationResponses
responseFields.description: Per-recipient results. A multi-recipient send can partially succeed, so branch on each entry's statusCode, not only the top-level one.

fields.name: address
fields.description: The tel:-prefixed recipient this entry reports on.

fields.name: messageId
fields.description: Per-recipient message identifier. Store it to match delivery reports.

fields.name: timeStamp
fields.description: When the platform processed this recipient.

rules: destinationAddresses is always an array.
Guard tel:all behind a deliberate, separately-authorised code path.
Keep under 160 GSM-7 characters for one part; Bengali is UCS-2, so budget 70. Every part is billed.
Only set deliveryStatusRequest to 1 if you consume the delivery-report callback.

services.name: USSD Send
services.summary: Send a USSD screen to a subscriber inside an active session.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Application ID as given when provisioned.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password given when provisioned.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: API version. Defaults to latest.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Screen text sent to the handset. ~182 char limit; assume 160.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Session number assigned by the USSD gateway. Echo the one the platform sent you; never generate your own.

parameters.name: ussdOperation
parameters.description: mt-init starts an app-initiated session, mt-cont keeps it open, mt-fin closes it.

parameters.name: destinationAddress
parameters.description: tel:-prefixed subscriber address; may be a hash key.

parameters.name: encoding
parameters.description: 440 = plain ASCII.

responseFields.name: requestId
responseFields.description: Uniquely identifies the request within bdapps.

rules: Echo the platform's sessionId. A wrong one orphans the session.
Terminal screens must use mt-fin, or the session hangs until the network times it out.
Plain ASCII only (encoding 440) — no emoji, no Bengali script, no smart quotes.
Reply fast: USSD sessions time out in seconds.

services.name: Subscription Register
services.summary: Opt a subscriber in to the application.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Application ID as received when provisioned.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password as received when provisioned.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: API version. Defaults to latest.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: 1 = opt in. Send the string "1".

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: tel:-prefixed subscriber address; may be masked.

responseFields.name: requestId
responseFields.description: Uniquely identifies the request within the SDP.

responseFields.name: subscriptionStatus
responseFields.description: REGISTERED, UNREGISTERED or PENDING. PENDING CHARGE means the subscriber has not been charged yet.

rules: Only call with explicit, recorded consent. Disclose amount and frequency before registering.
E1351 (already registered) is success — the desired state already holds.
A PENDING result is not active yet; wait for the subscription notification before delivering the service.

services.name: Subscription Unregister
services.summary: Opt a subscriber out of the application.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Application ID as received when provisioned.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password as received when provisioned.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: API version. Defaults to latest.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: 0 = opt out.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: tel:-prefixed subscriber address; may be masked.

responseFields.name: requestId
responseFields.description: Uniquely identifies the request within the SDP.

rules: Unregister must be as easy as register — offer it over MO SMS (STOP/UNSUB/OFF), USSD and in-app.
E1356 (not registered) is success — the desired state already holds.
Honour it immediately, including cancelling queued and scheduled messages.

services.name: Subscription Status
services.summary: Check the current subscription status of one subscriber.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Application ID as received when provisioned.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password as received when provisioned.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: tel:-prefixed subscriber address; may be masked.

rules: Use for reconciliation, not as a per-request gate — mirror state locally from the subscription notification instead.

services.name: Query Base (subscriber base size)
services.summary: Return the number of subscribers currently registered to the application.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Application ID as received when provisioned.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password as received when provisioned.

responseFields.name: baseSize
responseFields.description: Current subscriber base size. Arrives as a string — coerce before arithmetic.

rules: Needs no subscriber and costs nothing — the ideal connectivity and credential smoke test.
baseSize is a string. Parse it.
Poll on a schedule into your own metrics rather than per page load.
Sanity-check it before any tel:all broadcast.

services.name: OTP Request
services.summary: Dispatch a one-time PIN by SMS so a web or app user can be registered from a plain mobile number.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Application ID as received when provisioned.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password as received when provisioned.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: tel:-prefixed mobile number the user typed.

parameters.name: applicationHash
parameters.description: The hash string identifying your app, so bdapps sends the verification message in the form your app can read (the Android SMS Retriever app hash). It is a per-application constant, not a per-request id.

parameters.name: applicationMetaData
parameters.description: client (MOBILEAPP | WebSite | DESKTOP), device, os, appCode (package name / store URL / page URL / download URL).

responseFields.name: referenceNo
responseFields.description: Pass to OTP Verify. Keep server-side, in the session — never send it to the client.

rules: Rate-limit per number AND per IP, or the app becomes an SMS-bombing tool at your expense.
One OTP is valid for 60 minutes.
Always call from a backend with a static IP.

services.name: OTP Verify
services.summary: Verify a PIN and receive the masked subscriberId to use with every other API.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Application ID as received when provisioned.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password as received when provisioned.

parameters.name: referenceNo
parameters.description: From the OTP Request response. Server-side only.

parameters.name: otp
parameters.description: The PIN the user entered.

responseFields.name: subscriberId
responseFields.description: Masked subscriber identifier. Use this for SMS, Subscription and Charging from now on.

rules: Maximum 3 attempts per OTP — enforce it on your side too.
Never log the OTP or the referenceNo.
Store the returned masked subscriberId as the user's bdapps identity.

services.name: CaaS Direct Debit
services.summary: Charge a specific amount from a subscriber's mobile account. Moves real money.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Application ID generated when provisioning.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password authenticating the application.

parameters.name: externalTrxId
parameters.description: Your transaction ID, mapping request to response. Max 32 characters. Persist BEFORE calling — it is the idempotency key.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: MSISDN or hash key of the subscriber to charge.

parameters.name: paymentInstrumentName
parameters.description: The payment instrument to charge or read. MobileAccount is the only value bdapps accepts. Omitting it fails the call.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: Amount to charge, sent as a string. Hold as a decimal type in your own code.

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: The account of the payment instrument. Optional; a single value per request.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Currency of the amount. Only BDT is allowed.

responseFields.name: externalTrxId
responseFields.description: Echo of your ID. Assert it matches what you sent.

responseFields.name: internalTrxId
responseFields.description: Payment gateway transaction ID. Persist it — support and reconciliation use this.

responseFields.name: referenceId
responseFields.description: 8-digit number for the payment request, where an external charging menu is involved.

rules: The amount must be pre-agreed and disclosed to the user before they subscribe.
Persist externalTrxId before the HTTP call, then update the row from the response.
Never retry with a fresh externalTrxId — a timeout does not mean the charge failed.
E1379 (already completed) is success. E1406 (user rejected) must never be retried.
Amount and currency come from server-side config, never from client input.

services.name: CaaS Query Balance
services.summary: Query a subscriber's remaining chargeable balance.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Application ID generated when provisioning.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password authenticating the application.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: MSISDN or username of the subscriber being queried. The official sample omits the tel: prefix here, unlike every other service; send it tel:-prefixed for consistency — that is what works in practice.

parameters.name: paymentInstrumentName
parameters.description: The payment instrument to charge or read. MobileAccount is the only value bdapps accepts. Omitting it fails the call.

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: The account of the payment instrument. Optional; a single value per request.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Currency of the amount. Only BDT is allowed.

responseFields.name: chargeableBalance
responseFields.description: Remaining balance (prepaid) or credit limit minus outstanding bill (postpaid). A string — parse as decimal.

rules: Requires the Enable Query Balance Requests toggle in CaaS provisioning.
Advisory only — the balance can change before the debit lands. Always handle E1378 on the debit anyway.
chargeableBalance is a string — parse as decimal, never compare a float for equality.

callbacks.name: MO SMS Receive
callbacks.summary: Fires when a subscriber texts your shortcode with your keyword.

fields.name: applicationId
fields.description: Your application ID — verify it matches.

fields.name: sourceAddress
fields.description: Sender address, masked if masking is enabled.

fields.name: message
fields.description: Message as sent by the user, including the keyword.

rules: Recognise STOP / UNSUB / OFF and honour them by calling Unregister.
Do not perform a destructive or chargeable action on the content of one MO SMS alone.

callbacks.name: SMS Delivery Status Report
callbacks.summary: Final delivery state of an MT SMS sent with deliveryStatusRequest 1.

fields.name: timeStamp
fields.description: Time of the delivery event. Arrives as 10 digits (yyMMddHHmm) or 14 (yyyyMMddHHmmss) — parse on length.

fields.name: requestId
fields.description: Ties the report to the original send.

fields.name: deliveryStatus
fields.description: bdapps uses the long forms; the SMPP gateway uses the abbreviated ones. Accept both.

rules: ACCEPTED is not DELIVERED — it only means the network took the message.
Reports can arrive out of order, late, twice, or never.

callbacks.name: USSD Receive
callbacks.summary: Fires when a subscriber dials your code or presses a key.

fields.name: sessionId
fields.description: Session identifier — echo this back on every send.

fields.name: ussdOperation
fields.description: mo-init starts a session, mo-cont is subsequent input.

fields.name: message
fields.description: What the user dialled or typed.

rules: The response body is only an acknowledgement — the screen the user sees comes from a separate POST /ussd/send.
Sessions time out in seconds. Acknowledge before doing any work.

callbacks.name: Subscription Notification
callbacks.summary: Fires whenever a subscription changes, including changes you did not initiate.

fields.name: password
fields.description: Your application password, echoed back by the platform. You may compare it in constant time as defence in depth, but never log it and never treat it as sufficient authentication on its own — the request is unauthenticated JSON from the public internet.

rules: This is the authoritative source of subscription state — consume it and keep a local mirror instead of polling getStatus.
The body carries your password. Redact it before the payload reaches a log, an error tracker or a queue.

bdappsai.name: bdappsAI
bdappsai.summary: bdapps's AI gateway. One OpenAI-shaped API in front of several model providers — chat completions across Claude, Gemini and GPT models, and image generation — billed against a bdapps token balance instead of a per-provider account.
differsFromTelco: Credentials go in an Authorization HEADER, not in the JSON body. There is no applicationId and no password.
Failures come back as real HTTP status codes with an error object. There is no statusCode/S1000 envelope, so the telco branching rule is inverted here: on bdappsAI you DO check the HTTP status.
It is a separate product with a separate key and a separate balance. A bdapps application password will not authenticate a bdappsAI call, and a bdappsAI key will not authenticate an SMS send.
Nothing about it is Bangladesh-specific: there is no MSISDN, no tel: addressing, no operator and no subscriber.
Nothing about it is a callback. bdappsAI never calls you; there is no webhook to register.

auth.note: The whole value goes in the header verbatim, including the app_ prefix. It is not an OAuth bearer token: do not add the word Bearer, and do not base64-encode it. Generate and rotate the key in the bdappsAI portal.

models.note: Strongest general reasoning in the line-up. Use it where an answer's quality matters more than its latency — drafting, analysis, anything a subscriber reads.
Long-context reasoning. Use it for large documents and multi-step analysis. Preview: treat its availability and behaviour as less stable than the others.
Cheapest and fastest. Use it for classification, routing, short replies and anything on a USSD timer.
Small, fast and cheap with a newer base than gpt-4o-mini. A good default for high-volume short tasks.
Low-cost general model. A sensible default for chat where cost matters more than depth.
The only image model. Returns base64, never a URL.

rateLimits.onExceed: HTTP 429. Read the Retry-After header for the recommended wait, and back off exponentially with jitter rather than retrying immediately.
rateLimits.note: Quota is enforced two ways — requests per minute and total token spend. They surface as different error codes (RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and TOKEN_QUOTA_EXCEEDED) on the same 429, so read the code, not just the status.

error.param: Parameter name that caused the error (if applicable)

errorEnvelope.note: Read error.code first — it is the machine-readable one. error.message is for your logs, not for your branching, and error.param names the offending field on a 400.

services.name: bdappsAI Chat Completions
services.summary: Generate a model response for a conversation. OpenAI Chat Completions shape, routed to Claude, Gemini or GPT by the model field.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Which model answers. Each has different capabilities, performance characteristics and price points, and a model your project is not configured for fails with INVALID_LLM_CONFIG.

parameters.name: messages
parameters.description: The conversation so far, oldest first. Each entry has a role (system, developer, user, assistant or tool) and content, which is either a string or an array of typed parts — text, image and audio parts are supported.

parameters.name: temperature
parameters.description: Sampling temperature between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random; lower values make it more focused and deterministic. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: max_completion_tokens
parameters.description: An upper bound for the number of tokens that can be generated. Set it on every call: it is the only hard ceiling on what one request can cost you.

parameters.name: tools
parameters.description: A list of tools the model may call. The model replies with tool_calls instead of content, and you send the results back as messages with role tool.

parameters.name: response_format
parameters.description: The format in which the model output should be returned, such as { "type": "text" } or a JSON schema. Use it instead of asking for JSON in the prompt and parsing hopefully.

parameters.name: service_tier
parameters.description: Specifies the processing type used for serving the request. Defaults to auto.

parameters.name: frequency_penalty
parameters.description: Between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalise new tokens based on their existing frequency in the text so far, reducing verbatim repetition. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: logprobs
parameters.description: Whether to return log probabilities of the output tokens or not. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: How many chat completion choices to generate for each input message. Every choice is billed, so leave it at the default of 1 unless you genuinely use the alternatives.

parameters.name: presence_penalty
parameters.description: Between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalise new tokens based on whether they appear in the text so far, pushing the model towards new topics. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: prompt_cache_key
parameters.description: Groups requests that share a long identical prefix so the provider can cache it. Use a stable value per prompt template, never per user.

parameters.name: safety_identifier
parameters.description: A stable identifier used to help detect users violating usage policies. Send a hash of your own user id — never an MSISDN and never a subscriberId.

parameters.name: stop
parameters.description: Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating further tokens. Defaults to null.

parameters.name: store
parameters.description: Whether or not to store the output of this chat completion request. Defaults to false — leave it false for anything carrying subscriber data.

parameters.name: top_logprobs
parameters.description: The number of most likely tokens to return at each token position, 0 to 20. Requires logprobs to be true.

parameters.name: top_p
parameters.description: An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling. Defaults to 1. Adjust this or temperature, not both.

responseFields.name: id
responseFields.description: Identifier for this completion. Log it — it is what bdappsAI support traces a bad response by.

responseFields.name: created
responseFields.description: Unix timestamp of when the completion was created.

responseFields.name: model
responseFields.description: The model that actually answered. Check it rather than assuming your requested model was used.

responseFields.name: choices
responseFields.description: The generated alternatives, one per n. Each carries index, message, logprobs and finish_reason.

responseFields.name: choices[].message
responseFields.description: The assistant turn: role, content, refusal, annotations, and tool_calls when the model asked for a tool. Append it to your message history verbatim before the next turn.

responseFields.name: choices[].finish_reason
responseFields.description: Why generation stopped: stop is a complete answer, length means it hit max_completion_tokens and the content is truncated, tool_calls means the model wants a tool run. Branch on this — a truncated answer is not a failed request.

responseFields.name: usage
responseFields.description: Token accounting for this call: prompt_tokens, completion_tokens and total_tokens, plus cached and reasoning breakdowns. This is what draws down your balance, so record total_tokens per call.

responseFields.name: service_tier
responseFields.description: The processing tier that served the request.

content.text: You are a concise assistant for a Bangladeshi mobile service. Answer in one short paragraph.

message.content: Megapixels count the millions of pixels a photo contains…

rules: Call it from your backend only. The key is a bearer-equivalent secret with a spendable balance behind it; a browser or mobile app that holds it can drain the balance.
Always set max_completion_tokens. Without it a single runaway request can spend an unbounded share of your token balance.
Branch on the HTTP status here, unlike every telco endpoint in this catalog. There is no statusCode field and no S1000.
Check finish_reason before using the content. length means the answer is cut off mid-sentence.
Never put a raw MSISDN, a subscriberId or a bdapps password into a prompt, a safety_identifier or a prompt_cache_key. Prompts leave your trust boundary and reach a third-party model provider.
Retry only 429, 500, 502 and 503, with exponential backoff and jitter. A 400, 401, 402, 403 or 404 will fail identically forever.
Set an explicit client timeout well above your telco one — a large completion legitimately takes tens of seconds — and never make an LLM call inside a USSD callback's response path.
Treat model output as untrusted input: never execute it, never interpolate it into SQL or a shell, and never send it straight to a subscriber as an SMS without a length and content check.

services.name: bdappsAI Image Generation
services.summary: Create an image from a text prompt. GPT Image 1.5 only, and the image comes back as base64 in the response body rather than as a URL.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: A text description of the desired image(s). The maximum length is 32000 characters for GPT Image 1.5.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The image model to use. gpt-image-1.5 is the only one available and the default.

parameters.name: background
parameters.description: Background treatment. transparent requires an output_format of png or webp — it is silently useless with jpeg. Defaults to auto.

parameters.name: moderation
parameters.description: Content-moderation strictness for the generated image. Defaults to auto.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: How many images to generate, 1 to 10. Every image is billed separately. Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: output_compression
parameters.description: Compression level from 0 to 100 for the webp and jpeg output formats. Ignored for png. Defaults to 100.

parameters.name: output_format
parameters.description: The encoding of the returned image. Defaults to png.

parameters.name: quality
parameters.description: Rendering quality. This is the main cost and latency lever — low is dramatically cheaper and faster than high. Defaults to auto.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Dimensions of the generated image: square, landscape, portrait, or auto to let the model choose. Defaults to auto.

parameters.name: partial_images
parameters.description: Number of partial images, 0 to 3, to emit while generating. Only meaningful with stream set to true. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: stream
parameters.description: Generate the image in streaming mode, emitting partial images as server-sent events. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: Rendering style — vivid is more dramatic and saturated, natural is more literal. Defaults to vivid.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: A unique identifier representing your end-user, used for abuse monitoring. Send an opaque internal id, never an MSISDN.

responseFields.name: created
responseFields.description: Unix timestamp of when the image was created.

responseFields.name: data
responseFields.description: One entry per generated image. Each carries b64_json — the image bytes, base64-encoded. GPT Image 1.5 always returns base64, never a URL, so decode and store it yourself.

responseFields.name: output_format
responseFields.description: The encoding of the returned bytes — use it to pick the file extension and the Content-Type when you store or serve the image.

responseFields.name: quality
responseFields.description: The quality level actually used, which is the resolved value when you sent auto.

responseFields.name: size
responseFields.description: The dimensions actually produced, which is the resolved value when you sent auto.

responseFields.name: usage
responseFields.description: Token accounting: input_tokens with a text/image breakdown, output_tokens and total_tokens. Image output tokens dwarf the prompt, so quality and n drive the cost, not prompt length.

sampleRequest.prompt: a red apple on a plain background

rules: The response is base64, not a URL. Never log the body, never store it in a database text column, and never return it through a JSON API — decode it once and put the bytes in object storage.
Generation is slow. Do it in a background job and hand the user a job id, never inside a request the user is waiting on and never inside a callback handler.
quality and n set the price. Default to low for previews and thumbnails, and only spend high where the image is the product.
Cache by a hash of the resolved prompt plus every parameter. The same prompt costs the same again every time you ask.
transparent backgrounds need output_format png or webp; with jpeg the setting is quietly discarded.
Never send subscriber-identifying text in a prompt or in user.

400.description: Bad request — invalid request format or a malformed payload. Common causes are invalid JSON, missing required fields and invalid parameter values.
400.fix: Read error.param: it names the offending field. Validate the payload before sending rather than after failing.

401.description: Unauthorized. Your API key is either missing, invalid, or expired.
401.fix: Send the key verbatim as Authorization: app_<keyId>.<keyValue>. Do not prepend Bearer, do not base64-encode it, and check the value actually reached the process rather than being an empty environment variable.

402.fix: Top up the balance in the bdappsAI portal. Alert on this: it stops every AI call in the product, not one request.

403.description: Forbidden — insufficient permissions, or the model you asked for is restricted for your project.
403.fix: Check the project is ACTIVE and the model is enabled for it in the bdappsAI portal.

404.description: Not found — no project matches the API key you sent.
404.fix: Verify the key is a complete keyId.keyValue pair and belongs to the project you think it does. A truncated key looks exactly like a wrong one.

429.description: Too many requests — rate limit exceeded, or the token quota is exhausted. Please wait before making additional requests.
429.fix: Read the Retry-After header and back off exponentially with jitter. Check error.code: RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED clears on its own, TOKEN_QUOTA_EXCEEDED does not.

500.description: Internal server error — an unexpected error on the bdappsAI side. Their team is automatically notified of server errors.
500.fix: Retry with backoff, cap the attempts, then dead-letter and surface a degraded experience rather than hanging.

502.description: Bad gateway — bdappsAI failed to forward the request to the upstream LLM provider, usually provider downtime or connectivity.
502.fix: Retry with backoff, and consider failing over to another model: a 502 is usually one provider being down, not bdappsAI.

503.description: Service unavailable — temporarily down for maintenance or under high load.
503.fix: Retry with backoff. Check the provider status pages before escalating.

PROJECT_NOT_FOUND.description: Project not found with API key. The provided API key doesn't match any existing project.
PROJECT_NOT_FOUND.fix: Regenerate the key in the bdappsAI portal and confirm both halves of keyId.keyValue were copied.

PROJECT_INACTIVE.description: Project is not active. The project exists but its status is not ACTIVE.
PROJECT_INACTIVE.fix: Activate the project in the bdappsAI portal. No code change will help.

INVALID_LLM_CONFIG.description: Invalid LLM model. The specified model is not configured or allowed for your project.
INVALID_LLM_CONFIG.fix: Use a model enabled for the project. This is the bdappsAI equivalent of E1309 — provisioning, not payload.

RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.description: Rate limit exceeded. Your project has exceeded the allowed number of requests per time period.
RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.fix: Back off and retry; limits reset every minute. Queue bursts rather than firing them in parallel.

TOKEN_QUOTA_EXCEEDED.description: Token quota exceeded. Your project has used up its allocated token quota.
TOKEN_QUOTA_EXCEEDED.fix: Retrying will not clear this. Raise the quota or top up in the portal, and alert rather than looping.

INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE.description: Insufficient token balance. Your current balance is too low to process the request.
INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE.fix: Top up in the bdappsAI portal. Monitor the balance proactively so this never fires in production.

FORWARDING_FAILED.description: Failed to forward the request. The call to the upstream LLM provider failed due to connectivity or provider issues.
FORWARDING_FAILED.fix: Retry with backoff, or fail over to a model from a different provider.

practices.title: Treat the bdappsAI key like a payment key
practices.detail: It draws down a real token balance. Backend only, environment variable only, never in a client bundle, never in a log line, never in a committed file. Rotate it in the bdappsAI portal the moment it is exposed.

practices.title: Put a ceiling on every AI call
practices.detail: Set max_completion_tokens on every chat call and keep n at 1; keep image quality low and n at 1 unless the image is the product. Without a per-call ceiling one loop can exhaust the balance and take every AI feature down with a 402.

practices.title: Never put subscriber identity in a prompt
practices.detail: Prompts leave your trust boundary and reach a third-party model provider. No MSISDN, no subscriberId (masked or not), no bdapps password, no OTP. Redact before the call, and keep store false.

practices.title: Branch on the HTTP status for bdappsAI, on statusCode for telco
practices.detail: bdappsAI returns real HTTP status codes with an error object and no statusCode field; the telco APIs return HTTP 200 with statusCode. One shared HTTP helper that assumes either convention is wrong for half your calls. Keep the two clients separate.

practices.title: Never call a model inside a callback response path
practices.detail: USSD sessions time out in seconds and bdapps expects S1000 immediately. Acknowledge the callback first, generate out of band, then deliver the answer by SMS or on the next USSD screen.

practices.title: Treat model output as untrusted input
practices.detail: Never execute it, never interpolate it into SQL or a shell, and never forward it to a subscriber unchecked. An SMS built from a model response still costs money per part and still represents your brand.

configuration.action: Provisioning or credentials are wrong. Fix the portal — code changes will not help. Alert on these in production; the integration is down, not one request.

client.action: Your payload is wrong, or the user gave bad input. Fix the request or prompt the user.

user-state.action: The user is not eligible right now. Communicate; do not retry in a loop.

transient.action: Platform-side. Exponential backoff with jitter, capped attempts, then dead-letter.

practices.title: Never hardcode applicationId or password
practices.detail: Environment variables only, through one config module, validated at startup. Not in source, not in a client bundle, not in a committed file, not in a log, not in git history. Never prefixed NEXT_PUBLIC_ / VITE_ / REACT_APP_.

practices.title: Never call bdapps from client-side code
practices.detail: Clients call your backend; your backend calls bdapps. Credentials are a shared secret and the platform enforces IP whitelisting, which a mobile client cannot satisfy.

practices.title: Explicit consent before register or charge
practices.detail: Record who consented, when, through which channel, and the exact wording shown. Disclose amount, currency and frequency first. bdapps suspends applications over this.

practices.title: Charging must be idempotent
practices.detail: One externalTrxId per logical charge, persisted before the call, reused on retry. Never re-roll it — that double-charges a real person.

practices.title: Branch on statusCode, not the HTTP status
practices.detail: bdapps returns HTTP 200 for application-level failures. Checking res.ok reports failures as successes.

practices.title: Treat subscriberId as opaque
practices.detail: With masking enabled it is a hash, not a phone number. Do not parse it, strip it, or assume a length. Store and send back exactly what you received.

practices.title: Never ship rejectUnauthorized: false
practices.detail: Some hosts serve an incomplete certificate chain. Supply the missing intermediate CA explicitly; disabling verification exposes the credentials that can charge your subscribers.

practices.title: Acknowledge callbacks before doing work
practices.detail: Respond S1000 immediately, then process asynchronously. USSD sessions time out in seconds; slow handlers cause retries, duplicates and dropped sessions.

practices.title: Every callback handler must be idempotent
practices.detail: All four callbacks can arrive more than once. Deduplicate on the documented key. A duplicate subscription notification that flips a user's state twice, or a duplicate MO that answers a command twice, is a real bug.

practices.title: Never trust the callback body
practices.detail: It is unauthenticated JSON from the public internet. Validate the schema, verify applicationId, restrict by source IP, rate-limit, and never treat a callback as authorisation.

practices.title: A static egress IP is a hard requirement
practices.detail: IP whitelisting is enforced with E1303. Serverless platforms with rotating egress need a NAT gateway or fixed-IP proxy. Decide before choosing a host.

practices.title: Guard tel:all
practices.detail: A broadcast to the entire subscriber base must never be reachable from an ordinary code path. Require an explicit, separately-authorised call and sanity-check against Query Base first.

practices.title: USSD session state must be shared across instances
practices.detail: An in-process Map breaks the moment you scale horizontally or deploy. Use Redis or equivalent, with a ~2 minute TTL.

practices.title: Never log secrets or unmasked subscriber data
practices.detail: Log requestId, sessionId, externalTrxId and statusCode. Never the password, OTP, referenceNo, or an unmasked subscriberId. Mask in the logger, not at each call site.

practices.title: Set an explicit timeout on every call
practices.detail: 10-15 seconds. No default-infinite requests.

practices.title: Retry only transient codes and transport errors
practices.detail: Exponential backoff with jitter, capped attempts, then dead-letter. Never retry a definitive E13xx, and never retry a debit with a new externalTrxId.

practices.title: Mirror subscription state locally
practices.detail: Consume the subscription notification instead of calling getStatus on every request.

practices.title: Use a decimal type for money
practices.detail: Never a binary float. Amount and currency come from server-side config or a server-side price lookup, never from client input.

chargingSdk.name: Subscription Charging SDK
chargingSdk.summary: A signed browser redirect to a bdapps-hosted consent page. bdapps captures the subscriber's number, shows the amount and frequency, records consent, and activates the subscription and its charging — then returns the browser to a URL you nominate. It is not a library you install.
enablement: Sign in at https://user.bdapps.com and create a bdapps Pro application.
Provision the APIs you need — SMS and Subscription are both required for the SDK flow.
General → Advanced shows 'Enable Charging SDK', off by default and not switchable from the portal.
Email support@bdapps.com to have it enabled on that application.
Once enabled, the same Advanced section shows the API Key and API Secret.

auth.note: These are NOT the applicationId and password: the telco APIs reject the SDK pair, and the SDK rejects the telco pair.

parameters.name: apiKey
parameters.description: The API Key from General → Advanced. Travels in the query string; the secret never does.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: Your own unique id for this consent attempt. Persist it against the user's session BEFORE redirecting, and use it to match the return.

parameters.name: requestTime
parameters.description: Current UTC time, ISO-8601 with microseconds and a Z suffix (2026-08-25T09:41:22.481903Z). Part of the signature, so it must be the identical string in both places.

parameters.name: signature
parameters.description: sha512(apiKey|requestTime|apiSecret) as lower-case hex.

parameters.name: redirectUrl
parameters.description: Where bdapps returns the browser. HTTPS, and a URL you control — never built from user input.

rules: Build the URL and compute the signature on the server. A signature computed in browser JavaScript puts the API Secret in the bundle.
Generate requestTime once into a variable and use that variable in both the signature and the query string. Formatting it twice looks like a wrong secret.
URL-encode every parameter — requestTime contains ':' and redirectUrl contains '://'.
On return, look requestId up in your own store, then confirm the subscription with POST /subscription/getStatus. Never trust the redirect alone.
Mark requestId consumed so a replayed return cannot activate anything twice.
Record the consent — timestamp, requestId and what the user was shown.
The SDK does not replace the subscription APIs. Unregister, status and base size are still the JSON endpoints.
